lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- Holding the Room
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 5 -- Holding the Room

listenings.text: Most of what people call a hostile question is not hostile at all. It is a request to be reassured. Somebody in that room is going to have to defend your number in a conversation you will not be in, and they do not yet know how. The tone is sharp because they are worried, not because they are attacking you. And the mistake almost everyone makes is to answer the tone instead of the question. You defend yourself against an attack that was never there, and now the room has a defensive director and an unanswered question. Here is the thing nobody tells you early enough. Conceding a point costs you nothing and buys you everything. The person who concedes first is the one the room believes for the rest of the meeting. And keep it short. A long answer to a short question reads as doubt, whatever the words are.

Before I defend a position I ask myself one question, and it has saved me more meetings than any technique. Am I defending the decision, or am I defending myself? Those two feel identical from the inside and they are completely different from the outside. The sign that I have crossed the line is repetition. If I catch myself making the same argument in different words, I have stopped listening and I am just filling the room. That is digging in, and everybody can see it. Holding your ground looks different. You say the thing once, you give one piece of evidence, and then you are quiet and you let it sit. And when I genuinely do not have the answer, I park it out loud, with a date. I do not improvise something I will have to walk back next month. Changing your mind in the room costs you one meeting. Refusing to change it costs you the next three.

extra_audio.text: You are right that the pipeline was caught late. Where I would hold my ground is the premise. The loss ratio came down four points in the same quarter. If that still does not sit right, let us park it until Thursday.
